gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly identifies that fixed-radius mesh refinement converges only to finite-radius Dirichlet and Neumann-based quantities, not the whole-space eigenvalue, and that R must also tend to infinity. Its repair preserves the finite-radius limits and the lower correction, exactly matching the gold defect.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The convergence claim incorrectly treats h-refinement at fixed R as sufficient for convergence to the whole-space eigenvalue. Finite-radius truncation remains, and the lower endpoint retains its exterior correction; whole-space convergence requires R to tend to infinity as well.

component_coverage.gold_component: At fixed R, mesh refinement removes discretization and coefficient-approximation errors but the upper endpoint converges only to the finite-radius Dirichlet eigenvalue rather than the whole-space eigenvalue.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the fixed-R upper limit is lambda_k^R, explains that this need not equal lambda_k, and identifies the false fixed-mesh asymptotic claim.

component_coverage.gold_component: The lower endpoint remains a finite-radius Neumann-based bound with the exterior correction, so exact convergence to the whole-space eigenvalue requires R to tend to infinity as well.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly includes the Neumann-based corrected lower expression at fixed R and repairs the statement by requiring the joint h-to-zero and R-to-infinity limit.
